description: Free, no key needed: checks a timber request without solving it. Same arguments as optimize_wood (field descriptions there). Validate a wood request — free, no key, no quota, no solve. Schema-validate the SAME body `/v1/optimize/wood` takes, WITHOUT solving or spending a call. Warnings flag parts with no matching-section stock long enough. See `/v1/validate/2d`.

engine.description: As in 1D, `max` is not offered here (a **400** before a call is charged). `balanced` resolves to the same packer as `heuristic`: within a section a timber job is a length problem, and free nesting has nothing to offer it. The value is accepted, echoed back, and a warning states which packer actually ran.

include.description: Three kinds of token. NARROWING (`cutPlan`, `offcuts`): omit the field entirely to get both; a present array keeps only the narrowing tokens it lists (an empty array drops both). ADDITIVE EXPORT (`svg`, `csv`, `dxf`): each adds an inline export STRING to the response (`svg` a standalone 2D layout — 2D only, a warning is returned for 1D/wood; `dxf` an R12/AC1009 drawing; `csv` a cut list, RFC 4180 quoted (a part name with a comma or a quote stays one field) and formula-injection-guarded (a name beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, TAB or CR is prefixed with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet reads it as text, not a formula — CWE-1236). 2D DATA (`labels`, `planHash`, `pdf`, `labelsPdf`): `labels` adds per-piece label data (`labels[]`, see `Label2D`), `planHash` a 64-hex fingerprint of the plan (the same plan always gives the same hash), `pdf` the cutting-plan PDF and `labelsPdf` the label PDF, both base64-encoded and drawn by the same code as the CutOptim app. These four are 2D only: a 1D or wood request returns a `warnings` entry instead. `pdf` renders at most 500 parts (total quantity); a larger 2D request with `pdf` is a 413 `too_large` with `details.path: "include"`. Export and data tokens do not affect narrowing, so `["svg"]` adds svg and — listing no narrowing token — drops cutPlan/offcuts; use `["cutPlan","offcuts","svg"]` to keep everything.

options.description: Identical to `Options1D` — a cross-section changes what fits, not how a bar is cut.

parts.description: The timber parts to cut, one row per part type: cross-section `sw` × `sh`, `length`, optional `qty`.

stock.description: At most 50 rows. Since every cross-section needs at least one stock row, this is also the practical ceiling on cross-sections in a single job; a wider catalogue should be split into several requests.
